description: The script prep run pubsub-21156937744383149 shipped on 2026-09-10 (prompt v9, $0.19, 4.5 min to the gate) after one redraft the voice lint asked for (an 18-word hook, a 16-word sentence). input.topic: Why we cap a short-form video at $2 to produce: what a two-dollar budget forces a marketing team to decide first

voiceRules.tone: clear and precise, confident without being arrogant

endorsedOutput.hook: We cap every short at two dollars to produce. On purpose.
endorsedOutput.formatRationale: The concept has a concrete place in it (the production context, the empty studio, the decision before the shoot) so real footage gives the argument texture that a text-led layout would flatten.

beats.narration: We cap every short at two dollars to produce. On purpose.
beats.visualBrief: A single coin resting on a worn wooden table surface, late-afternoon window light raking across the grain. Shot directly overhead, tight frame. No text, no hands, no other objects.

beats.narration: You can't hide behind a beautiful shot at two dollars. You have to know your point first.
beats.visualBrief: A small empty studio, two softboxes switched off, black backdrop partly rolled up, a folded tripod leaning against the wall. Overhead fluorescent light. No people, no screens, no text.
beats.stockQuery: empty film studio softbox lights tripod

beats.narration: The cap forces two questions. Who is this for? What do you want them to do?
beats.visualBrief: A long conference table, no people, a dry-erase marker resting on the whiteboard ledge, morning light from a row of windows on one side. Wide shot, clean and still. No text on the whiteboard.

beats.narration: Most video spend buys production. Not clarity. The two-dollar cap is a strategy tool.
beats.visualBrief: Bare concrete warehouse floor, a single overhead industrial lamp illuminated, the rest of the space in deep shadow. Wide shot, early morning. No people, no text, no machinery in frame.

endorsedOutput.caption: A production budget doesn't tell you what to say. That decision comes first. The $2 cap keeps the strategy question from getting buried under production decisions. karoslabs.com. No pitch, just a plan. #ContentStrategy #AIMarketing #CMO #KarosLabs
endorsedOutput.about: This short explains Karos Labs' internal $2 short-form video production cap as a strategic forcing function, not a cost constraint. It argues that stripping out budget pressure forces clarity on audience and intent before a single frame is shot. Four beats, 24 seconds, voiceover. No CTA in the video itself; CTA lives in the caption.
endorsedOutput.voiceoverRationale: This piece is an explanation with a 'because' in it: a mechanism (the cap forces a decision) and a turn (production is not the point). A spoken voice carries the logical sequence; captions alone would read as a list.

sources: Karos Labs production rule (2026-09-09): every original short is capped at $2 to produce, enforced by the workflow's cost ceiling.
